hints: Resolve the four coplanar forces into two perpendicular directions: vertically and horizontally.
Set the net vertical force to zero: $G\sin 60^\circ + 2F\sin 40^\circ - 10 = 0$.
Set the net horizontal force to zero: $F + G\cos 60^\circ - 2F\cos 40^\circ = 0$, express $G$ in terms of $F$, and solve simultaneously.
walkthrough:
State the equilibrium conditions for coplanar forces: the sum of resolved components along any two perpendicular directions must be zero:
$$\sum F_x = 0\quad\text{and}\quad\sum F_y = 0$$

Resolve forces vertically (taking upwards as positive):
- Force $G$: $+G\sin 60^\circ$
- Force $2F$: $+2F\sin 40^\circ$
- Force $10\text{ N}$: $-10$
- Horizontal force $F$: $0$
Set the sum to zero:
$$G\sin 60^\circ + 2F\sin 40^\circ - 10 = 0 \quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

Resolve forces horizontally (taking rightwards as positive):
- Force $F$: $+F$
- Force $G$: $+G\cos 60^\circ$
- Force $2F$: $-2F\cos 40^\circ$
- Vertical force $10\text{ N}$: $0$
Set the sum to zero:
$$F + G\cos 60^\circ - 2F\cos 40^\circ = 0 \quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

Rearrange Equation 2 to express $G$ in terms of $F$:
$$G\cos 60^\circ = 2F\cos 40^\circ - F = F(2\cos 40^\circ - 1)$$
Since $\cos 60^\circ = 0.5$:
$$G = \frac{F(2\cos 40^\circ - 1)}{0.5} = 2F(2\cos 40^\circ - 1)$$

Substitute $G$ into Equation 1:
$$[2F(2\cos 40^\circ - 1)]\sin 60^\circ + 2F\sin 40^\circ = 10$$
Factor out $F$:
$$F \left[2(2\cos 40^\circ - 1)\sin 60^\circ + 2\sin 40^\circ\right] = 10$$
Calculate intermediate numerical values:
$$2\cos 40^\circ - 1 = 2(0.766044) - 1 = 0.532089$$
$$2(0.532089)\sin 60^\circ = 1.064178 \times 0.866025 \approx 0.921606$$
$$2\sin 40^\circ = 2(0.642788) \approx 1.285575$$
Sum of the coefficients:
$$0.921606 + 1.285575 = 2.207181$$
$$2.207181F = 10$$
Divide both sides by $2.207181$:
$$F = \frac{10}{2.207181} \approx 4.5307\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $F = 4.53\text{ N}$.

Substitute $F = 4.5307\text{ N}$ back to find $G$:
$$G = 2(4.5307)(0.532089) = 4.8214\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $G = 4.82\text{ N}$.

hints: The $10\text{ N}$ force acts along the vertical axis. For the resultant to be perpendicular to this force, the resultant must be horizontal, meaning the net vertical component is zero.
Set the sum of components parallel to the $10\text{ N}$ force to zero: $G\sin 60^\circ + 2F\sin 40^\circ - 10 = 0$.
walkthrough:
Interpret the geometric condition: the $10\text{ N}$ force acts vertically downwards. If the resultant force of the system is perpendicular to the $10\text{ N}$ force, the resultant must be purely horizontal.
Therefore, the vertical component of the resultant must be zero:
$$\sum F_y = 0$$

Write the vertical component balance with $F = 3\text{ N}$:
$$G\sin 60^\circ + 2F\sin 40^\circ - 10 = 0$$
Substitute $F = 3$:
$$G\sin 60^\circ + 2(3)\sin 40^\circ - 10 = 0$$
$$G\sin 60^\circ + 6\sin 40^\circ = 10$$

Divide both sides by $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866025$:
$$G = \frac{6.14327}{0.866025} \approx 7.0936\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $G = 7.09\text{ N}$.
